preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. You are working at a long-term care facility and find a 69-year-old female patient is feeling unwell and is complaining of hot, red, and swollen legs. You suspect cellulitis so send for a bacterial culture.

preamble.title: The case - Mr. Jenning
preamble.html: The case. Mr. Jenning is a 78-year-old man who presents to the emergency department after a fall in his retirement home. He has a history of hypertension, vascular dementia, Type 2 diabetes, osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, atrial fibrillation, benign prostatic hypertrophy, bladder outlet obstruction, and COPD. He also had a transient ischemic attack five years ago. His daughter is present at the bedside and says that on several occasions in the last few days Mr. Jenning “had not been himself”. He had rambling speech, appeared to be confused, and asked her the same questions repeatedly. His daughter also notes that in the last year her father had several episodes of “confusion” involving word-finding difficulty and slurred speech.

preamble.title: The case - Mr. Johnson
preamble.html: The case. Mr. Johnson’s comorbidities are T2DM, COPD, HTN, Osteopenia, Chronic lower back pain, TIA, BPH, Depression, Hypertriglyceridemia, Hypothyroidism. His medications are Aspirin, Ramipril, Citalopram, Rosuvastatin, Acetaminophen, Calcium, Finasteride, Levothyroxine, Ventolin inhaler, Metformin, Vitamin D, Symbicort inhaler. During morning rounds, you check in with Mr. Johnson. He describes feeling unwell with right upper quadrant pain, and seems confused. You manage to learn from his wife that a bumbling incompetent clerk came in two nights ago and gave her husband a handful of pills that all looked the same. The clerk left the next morning without checking on Mr. Johnson and is not responding to text messages. preamble.title: The case - Tony
preamble.html: The case. Tony is a 77 year old male who is taken to the ER by his son in law after a fall in his long term care home. Since the fall he has been quite drowsy and confused. He is able to name his age, date of birth but not the current year. When asked to name the months of year in backwards order he achieves 9 of the months correctly. He has a history of Type 2 diabetes, myocardial infarction, generalized anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder. His family history is positive for colorectal cancer and Dementia. At baseline he is able to perform most ADLs independently but requires help with several IADLs including paying bills, and grocery shopping.

preamble.title: The case - Sasha
preamble.html: The case. Sasha, age 65 was diagnosed with a primary lung cancer that has metastasized to her liver and stomach. Today she presents with acute dyspnea as well as some chest pain and coughing. On physical exam you find facial edema and thoracic vein distension.

preamble.title: The case - Willow
preamble.html: The case. Willow, a 74 year old woman presents with chronic dyspnea that worsens with activity and settles partially with rest. Her dyspnea is a source of moderate anxiety, and she recognizes that her anxiety worsens her dyspnea. Due to her dyspnea she is unable to walk her pet cat or contribute to much house work. She occasionally relies on her husband to help her with bathing and toileting. In your exam room her breathing is mildly laboured and and she pauses while talking every ~30 seconds while you take a history.
